bigtext.summary: All 5 variants scored 4/5. Fixed: entrance clipping (1.8x stamp overflowed canvas), Shorts safe-area overrun, 350ms hard colour pop, hardcoded glitch hex, Math.random nondeterminism, icon flying through headline, v0 accent bar at full opacity at t=0, v2 letters cascading through the icon, 3D grid hardcoded hex. Harness gained --scene= and --entrance to get here.

bullets.summary: 1/2/3/1/4 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Found the systemic frozen-3D-layer bug here (29 painters). Also fixed: half the bullets under the Shorts UI band, 16:9 slicing its outer panels (spreadY exceeded the frustum), labels overflowing their panels, sheared off-axis camera, dead rowGap.

quote.summary: 2/4/4/4/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Glass card overhung both side edges at 9:16 (blockW half 3.0 vs frustum halfW 2.87); now clamped via the new frustumHalfExtent helper. Measured 0% edge bleed after. Hardcoded grid hex removed.

stat.summary: 1/2/2/3/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Fixed: isoCamera frustum overflow at 9:16 (blockW hardcoded 5.8 vs halfW 1.81), context text overlapping a 2-line label, label fading in over still-spinning odometer reels, 2 hardcoded hex.

steps.summary: 3/4/4/4/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. List was centred in the full content box, pushing it low with a dead third under the title; now centred in the visible band above the Shorts UI. 2 hardcoded hex removed. NOTE: ~174 lines of uncommitted 3D-staircase work in this file were destroyed by an unguarded git checkout on 2026-07-27; this is the committed 2D version.

vocab.summary: 2/3/4/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. 3D slabs and example text were unrelated layers (off-axis camera + per-row Z stagger vs text centred on the projected origin). Front-on camera, coplanar rows, card size from frustumHalfExtent, text box from the projected front face. Killed a 26%-of-frame dead void, aligned empty sockets to their cards, replaced an off-frame entrance slide with a scale, 4 hardcoded hex. 0% edge bleed both aspects.

mythfact.summary: 1/2/3/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Card chrome (chip/text/badge/strike) was a pixel rect sized from contentW then re-centred on the projected block, so on 16:9 the chip and first line floated in black off the slab and the badge sat 120px past its edge. Front-on coplanar blocks sized from frustumHalfExtent; chrome rect derived from the projected front face. Also: bust colour ramps over 320ms instead of flipping in one frame, strike spans the measured text not the card width, emphasis variant now reaches the geometry, faces darkened for text contrast, 5 hardcoded hex. 0% edge bleed both aspects.

dialogue.summary: 1/1/2/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The scene rendered ZERO message text on every frame after the first: projectedPoints was a per-paint array filled inside build()'s update() closure, which captures frame 0's array, so the live one stayed empty and every bubble was dropped. Realigned the 3D layer to the 2D layout with an axis-aligned camera (projectToRect is affine on a z=const plane, so pixel<->world round-trips exactly); removed the two-axis group wobble. Also: accentSoft/rgba() into THREE.Color dropped alpha and rendered a solid sky-blue slab; edge wireframes now fade with their face; short threads centre instead of pinning to the bottom of an empty panel; 5 hardcoded hex. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

terminal.summary: 2/3/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Top-down camera keystoned the slab while the title bar / traffic lights / body text are axis-aligned pixel rects taken from the bounding box of two projected corners, so the bar overhung the slab's top-right corner into black. Window is now upright before an axis-aligned camera, sized from the frustum, chrome on the projected front face. Also dropped the slab scale+bob that slid under fixed-pixel chrome, sized the window to its content so it clears the Shorts UI band (was running to y=1745), raised the mono cap for phone legibility, removed 2 rgba()-into-THREE.Color calls + 9 hardcoded literals. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

storyboard.summary: 2/3/3/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Top-down camera + a 2D card rect taken from the bounding box of two projected corners: every slab keystoned while its card stayed axis-aligned, so margins differed per row, panels were unequal sizes, and the lit top faces read as silver bars. Pixel grid is now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its exact cell via an axis-aligned camera. Also clamped the grid above the Shorts UI band (bottom caption was at y=1690), removed the easeOutBack reveal scale that shrank 1.0->0.9 before growing back and the active-panel y-bob, one absolute card inset on all sides, 2 rgba()-into-THREE.Color calls + 8 hardcoded literals gone. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

question.summary: 1/4/4/3/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The whole 2D layer was translated by the unclamped projection error of an off-axis camera, slicing the heading at x=0 and the CTA at the bottom edge; now clamped. CTA also moved above the Shorts UI band. Measured 0% edge bleed after.

quiz.summary: 2/2/3/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Same frozen-local-array bug as dialogue: projectedPoints filled inside build()'s update() closure, so every option's badge/label/tick was dropped from frame 1 on. 3D layer realigned to the 2D layout via an axis-aligned camera; group wobble removed; option text shrinks to fit instead of wrapText()[0] silently truncating 52-char options; edge wireframes fade with their face; 7 hardcoded hex/rgba gone including an rgba() string passed to THREE.Color. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed. NOTE: the think-time countdown HUD is unreachable in the probe (needs a gap between beat windows) and was not exercised.

code.summary: 1/3/3/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The editor window overflowed BOTH side edges at 9:16 (traffic lights half off at x=0, JS badge and UTF-8 clipped, code cut mid-string; edge-check 1.7% left): the 3D viewport was the whole frame with a hardcoded 7.5-wide block against a ~3.49 frustum half-width, and the pixel chrome was scaled onto the block by the MEAN of its two axis scales. Viewport is now the window itself, block sized from that frustum, chrome drawn in plain pixels with no transform. edge-check 1.7% -> 0.0%. Also dropped bob + two-axis rotation + easeOutBack overshoot, clamped above the Shorts UI band, removed 11 hardcoded literals including 3 that hardcoded the default sky accent and ignored the subject palette.

trace.summary: 1/3/4/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Same defect as code: 3D viewport was the whole frame with a hardcoded 7-wide block against a ~3.49 frustum half-width, chrome fitted to it by the MEAN of two axis scales -> 1.5% left edge bleed at 9:16. Viewport is now the panel rect, block sized from that frustum, chrome in plain pixels. Also dropped group offset/scale/bob/rotation, clamped the array-cell band to the Shorts UI edge (it centred in a band running past it, leaving ~200px dead space under the code panel), 2 hardcoded hex. edge-check 1.5% -> 0.0%.

memgrid.summary: 1/2/2/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. A uniform memory grid rendered as six different shapes with the outer columns off both frame edges: cell positions were world literals on a ground plane under a camera at (0,12,10), so every cell sat at a different depth while the 2D chrome used one fixed pixel width. Pixel grid is now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its cell via an axis-aligned camera. SEPARATELY the 3D cell colours were frozen at frame 0 (update() read the painter-local writes/frees/cur captured by the build closure) so allocation/write/free were invisible in 3D — that state now travels through render3D's context arg. Also accentSoft (an rgba string) into THREE.Color.setStyle rendered as full accent, grid now clears the Shorts UI band, ptr pin moved inside its own cell (was landing on the next row's address), 5 hardcoded literals. edge-check 0.5% -> 0.0%.

callstack.summary: 2/3/1/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The 3D stack showed ONE slab for the whole scene: update() read the painter-local cur/prev/pushing/popping captured by the build closure on frame 0, so push and pop never reached the 3D layer; that state now travels through render3D's context arg. Frame slabs were world literals under a camera at (0,4,14) while labels were pixel rows — pixel rows are now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its row via an axis-aligned camera, and the 2D row matches the push/pop scale so the label no longer overhangs a half-grown slab. Also: stack base was clamped to h*0.86 (baseline + bottom frame under the Shorts UI) -> 0.75; rows fill their band instead of a third of it; per-frame bob gone; accentSoft no longer handed to THREE.Color.setStyle; 3 hardcoded hex.

circuit.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: hex.slice is not a function (painters/circuit.ts:197 passes 4 args to a 2-arg helper) — every frame errors

chart.summary: Containment/typography already good (own CAPTION_SAFE_Y, 0% measured bleed). Fixed 5 hardcoded hex. HELD AT 3 ON MOTION: nothing but the title is solid for the whole first 500ms - grid/labels sit at ~15% opacity and no column appears. Partly a probe artifact (probe opens beat 0 at p=0.05 = 2.4s; engine opens it at t=0), so needs that ruled out before fixing. radar.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: cy is not defined — every frame errors

diagram.summary: 2/3/3/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Pixel layout made authoritative (11th painter on the systemic 2d-layout-round-tripped-through-camera pattern): rects were recovered by projecting a world box through a tilted camera, so every node drew a second misregistered copy and adjacent grid rows collapsed into overlaps that hid the arrows. The correct pixel grid (gridMap/nodeRect) was already in the file as dead code; revived it, camera on-axis at (0,0,12), slabs placed from the pixel rect via mappingAt. Bottom clamp layout.h*0.86 (duplicated in two places) -> caption-aware layout.safeBottom; 9:16 lowest row was at 87% of frame height. Accent-node entrance flash removed (slab face was full accent under a fading 2D card; now one shared opacity ramp and a 0.22 tint). Per-node state moved from closure capture to render3D context - positions and highlights were frozen at frame 0. Slab bob/lift removed per the systemic rule. Arrow labels search along and across the route (writes was painted over the word Database). 9:16 transpose no longer mirrors reading order. 11 colour literals -> 0, two of which were rgba() passed to THREE.Color which drops alpha, so the dimming silently never happened; console.log went from 18 warnings to empty. Absolute-px lineWidth=1 and shadowOffsetY=4 gone. ~60 lines of dead code removed. edge-check 0.0% both aspects. Not covered by any demo fixture: scenes with step.move.

zoomladder.summary: Edge bleed is INTENTIONAL (final rung is Earth filling the frame) - do not clamp. Real defect: the scale caption renders at y~1700, inside the Shorts UI band (>1440), so the label naming the rung is hidden on 9:16. Also a hard black box seam where the 3D rect starts. See qa/zoomladder/FINDINGS.md.

dayclock.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: reading translate of undefined (painters/dayclock.ts:135,140 read .geometry off a THREE.Group) — every frame errors

compare.summary: 2/4/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. All three layout variants verified for the first time: both fixtures used the id sqlnosql (variantOf -> 0), so 2 of 3 layouts had never been rendered. New DEMO_COMPARE_VARIANTS (restgrpc, tcpudp) reaches them via --scene=. Variant 2 (stacked at 16:9) proved unusable - ~180px per panel, less than the header needs before one item draws, so every item in both panels was dropped; variantOf(id,3) -> variantOf(id,2), 16:9 always side-by-side with divider as the variety. Panels were placed by two unrelated systems (pixel rect vs world literals spreadX*1.5), putting the chrome ~85px off its own slab; slabs now sized and placed FROM the panel rects via mappingAt (12th painter on the systemic pattern) and the forbidden per-frame bob is gone. Verdict was drawn at 86% (9:16) / 90% (16:9) of frame height, inside the caption band -> layout.safeBottom, and verdictBand 3.2u -> 4.0u since a two-line box needs 3.84u. Side-by-side took the whole band whatever it held (~40% empty) -> height from content, pair centred; the right panel's y read panelsTop where the left read blockTop. Item block now scales to fit (floor 0.72 ~ 31px) so the schema's max of 4 items fits a stacked 9:16 panel. The isCurrent glow was dead code - shadowBlur set then zeroed on the next line - so the active side had no distinction. Verdict tick was prefixed to every wrapped line. 4 colour literals -> 0 plus two rgba() strings handed to THREE.Color which drops alpha (console.log 2 warnings/frame -> empty). Dead get2D and the tilted-camera floor grid removed. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

showdown.summary: Side labels/scores/crown clipped off both edges at 9:16. Root cause identified: 2D pixel layout mapped linearly to world (spreadX 5.5) then projected back through a camera at (0,10,7) - does not round-trip, and 9:16 frustum halfW is only ~2.23. Needs a layout rework (derive spread from the camera), NOT a clamp. See qa/showdown/FINDINGS.md.

systemic.detail: render3D caches the ThreeBundle per key; painters wrote update() as a closure over env, capturing frame 0. Every scene starts at p=0, so the whole 3D layer was frozen/invisible in production. Fixed in three3d.ts via a liveEnv arg + Object.assign onto the captured env; all 29 call sites updated. VISUALLY VERIFIED ONLY FOR bigtext AND bullets - the other 27 now animate for the first time and must be re-reviewed as the wave reaches them. ALSO: liveEnv only refreshes `env`. Painters whose update() reads OTHER painter-local values (Sets, derived state, output arrays) are still frozen at frame 0 — confirmed and fixed in memgrid (write/free colours) and dialogue/quiz (projectedPoints). Pass such state through render3D's `context` argument instead.

Geometry is built once per key from the first rect it sees, so rendering short then long in one page reused the wrong build. Harmless in production (one aspect per video) but it corrupted QA. probe now calls resetThree3D() before every strip.

Painters size three.js geometry with literals that only fit 16:9; the frustum half-width is halfH*aspect, so 9:16 is ~2.5x narrower and the geometry hangs off both edges. Hit bullets, stat and quote. three3d.ts now exports frustumHalfExtent(camera, rect) - use it instead of literals. npm run edge-audit measures which kinds still bleed.

Painters that map 2D pixel positions linearly into world space and then project back through a TILTED perspective camera do not recover the source pixel - the ground plane maps non-linearly. Confirmed in showdown; suspected in race and any painter with a worldPos(px,py) helper plus an off-axis camera. Symptom: elements near the design edges land outside the frame, worst at 9:16 where the frustum is narrowest. FIX PATTERN (applied to vocab, mythfact, dialogue, quiz, terminal, storyboard, code, trace, memgrid, callstack on 2026-07-27; diagram and compare on 2026-08-01): make the PIXEL layout authoritative and put the camera on-axis at (0,0,D). projectToRect is then affine on any z=const plane, so a local mappingAt(camera, z) -> {origin, pxPerWorldX, pxPerWorldY} gives an exact invertible pixel<->world map; size each slab as pixelRect/scale and place it at toWorld(pixelRect centre). Never scale/rotate/bob the 3D group afterwards — the pixel chrome cannot follow it.

Same root cause as frozen-3d-layer but the frozen value is a painter-local array the update() closure writes INTO, not env. The central liveEnv fix cannot reach it. In dialogue this suppressed 100% of the message text. Grep for a const array declared in the painter body and mutated inside build()'s update(). Confirmed in quiz.ts:99/205/221 by the same grep.

tools.name: edge-audit
tools.detail: Renders every kind at both aspects, diffs a 3px border ring against the bare background, flags hard-contrast content at the frame edge. Writes qa/AUDIT.md. Measures rubric section 1 across all 110 kinds in ~4 min instead of reading 220 contact sheets.
